title: Mapping-simplex presentations and their marked equivalence criterion
statement:
Use simplicial sets and categorical equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and marked objects, Cartesian fibrations and the model $\mathsf M_S$ of [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model]. Let $n\geq0$ and let $A_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow A_n$ be a chain of small simplicial sets. Its marked mapping simplex $M^m(A)\to\Delta^n$ has $r$-simplices $(\alpha,a)$, where $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$ is monotone and $a\in(A_{\alpha(r)})_r$. For $\theta:[s]\to[r]$, first apply $\theta^*$ to $a$, then apply the chain transition $A_{\alpha(r)}\to A_{\alpha\theta(s)}$; this gives the operator on the second coordinate. An edge $(\alpha,a)$ is marked exactly when $a$ is degenerate in $A_{\alpha(1)}$. Its vertex fiber at $i$ is $A_i^\flat$.
Every small Cartesian fibration $Y\to\Delta^n$ admits such a chain and a marked map $q:M^m(A)\to Y^\natural$ whose maps $A_i\to Y_i$ on all vertex fibers are categorical equivalences. Every marked map $q$ with this fiberwise property is a Cartesian equivalence in $\mathsf M_{\Delta^n}$. Equivalently the fiberwise hypothesis can be expressed by requiring $A_i^\flat\to Y_i^\natural$ to be a weak equivalence in the absolute marked model. The assertions include $n=0$ and empty fibers, and do not assert that $M^m(A)$ is fibrant.
